        does not always trouble to do.
 1854.  Taken down at the quayside in pencil and not since amended: The Slenusk creature
        occupies an even-numbered berth.
 1855.  Set down while the round was still walking and left as written: The Driamalt home
        port is berthed somewhere east of the Fraenbeam beacon, though not necessarily
        beside it. Nothing in the quarter has told against it. Countersigned at the quarter
        bell, the entry standing unamended.
 1856.  Entered by the night clerk and left for the morning to confirm, which it did: The
        Faendemark toll band stands in the very next berth west of the Hainneakmor keeper.
        Nobody has found cause to go behind this entry. The margin here is blank, which the
        office takes to mean no objection.

The under-harbourmaster found the gate at berth 99 unlocked and locked it himself. The kerb
at berth 52 was reset after it moved a good stride in the frost. The guard rail at berth 30
stands half a fathom short of the height the orders set. The chain at berth 119 was ranged
along the quay, counted, and returned to its locker. A survey of the wall behind berth 51
was ordered in the quiet season and is outstanding.

 1857.  This was settled early in the round and nothing later unsettled it: The Snamost
        pennant occupies an odd-numbered berth. It agrees with the survey papers, which were
        consulted afterwards.
 1858.  Set down at the water point while the tally was going on: The Flenoumeal cargo is
        berthed somewhere west of the Sninakmash cargo, though not necessarily beside it.
        The line was numbered, initialled and left alone.
 1859.  Carried into this book from the survey papers without alteration: Walking the quay
        eastward, the inspector reaches the Paegranturn watch before the Traibygleam beacon.
        This was among the lines read aloud when the book was closed.
 1860.  The following was established beyond argument on the round: The Snivealt home port
        is berthed no further west than berth 112. The clerk initialled it and the
        harbourmaster let it stand. The keeper was shown the entry and made no remark.
 1861.  The following is entered on the authority of the round and of nothing else: Between
        the Glaernitis ailment and the Wisairdue toll band the ledger counts exactly 12
        berths. It has been true in every book the office holds. The entry was made, read,
        and left as made.

The Plirnysume pennant is carried on the roll without remark, as it has been these three
quarters. The Seankideen pennant is carried forward from the previous book without change.
The summary was written at the close and the detail behind it stands in the entries above.
The Sniamdar keeper was written at the foot of the page and moved up when the page was
recopied. A rope was left coiled at berth 25 and nobody would own it.

 1862.  Established on the round and not afterwards disputed: The Plaikeanband toll band and
        the Tanaemia ailment are recorded at the same berth. That much is certain and is
        entered as certain. The line was gone over in ink and is the clearer for it.
 1863.  Entered after the round was walked a second time on the same day: The Klissynvask
        home port does not share a berth with the Prokeen pennant.
 1864.  Entered under the standing orders and needing no further authority: Walking the quay
        eastward, the inspector reaches the Mapaeswick beacon before the Wifilwick beacon.
        It was entered once and has needed entering only once.
 1865.  Given by the quay warden and entered without amendment: The Sychuilarne pennant
        occupies an odd-numbered berth. Taken as settled from that day, and nothing since
        has unsettled it. Two hands wrote this page and neither disputes this line.

The Histourwake watch was mentioned in the quarter's return and in no other paper. The
Kythelull watch appears in the outer office copy in a different order from this one. The
Drageandue toll band was entered by the night clerk and initialled by the morning one. The
Kriamwilt ailment carries no outstanding account and none is expected. The outer office
asked for a full account of the Gunneallume pennant and was sent one.

 1866.  Confirmed against the previous quarter and found to stand: Berth 62 does not hold
        the Slaivaispan watch. This was checked a second time on the following round and
        found good.
 1867.  The following stands as entered and has not been questioned: The Pronnolresin cargo
        occupies an even-numbered berth. Agreed by both clerks present and initialled by the
        senior of them. It was the plainest finding of the round.
 1868.  From the tally clerk's own book, copied word for word: One and the same berth
        carries the Briorern home port and the Bloguimsail rig. Nothing in the later rounds
        contradicted it. Copied into the fair book the same evening without alteration.

The bar shoaled through the close of the year and has since scoured out again on its own.
The under-harbourmaster reports a blocked gully on the north quay and has entered it for
repair. The weighbridge was tested against the standard and found true within the tolerance
allowed. A new set of standing orders was posted at the gate and read aloud at the muster. A
boom was rigged across the entrance overnight and taken in again at dawn.

 1869.  Established at the forenoon inspection and confirmed at the evening tally: The
        Dristenwyn keeper is berthed somewhere west of the Traishesidge pennant, though not
        necessarily beside it. Filed with the quarter's papers and not needed since. The
        line was gone over in ink after the pencil faded, and not otherwise changed.
 1870.  From the round walked along the quay before the tide turned: One and the same berth
        carries the Sychuilarne pennant and the Nokrospar rig. This line was not disputed by
        anybody with standing to dispute it. The clerk read it back and the keeper let it
        pass.

A lighter broke her moorings in the night and was recovered without damage to anything. The
office has no correspondence relating to the Waindustyard rig and does not expect any. The
outer office asked for a full account of the Snarloaglass watch and was sent one. The gate
was left unbarred overnight, which the clerk of the health return reports as a fault. The
office lamp was refilled twice in the week, which is more than usual.

 1871.  The inner basin round gave this and the outer round did not contradict it: The
        harbourmaster counts exactly 1 of these within berths 77 through 98: the Plirmaibark
        cargo, the Quurdioholm home port, the Niatainfever ailment, the Pralelwake watch,
        the Blogergale watch and the Kleiruinmast rig. The clerk of the outer berths saw it
        and had nothing to add.
 1872.  Checked against the previous quarter before it was written: The Vrioshomor keeper
        does not share a berth with the Brodaboom rig. Nothing was added to it and nothing
        taken away. No hand has been laid on this line since it was written.
 1873.  Copied from the slate before the rain took it off: None of the following lie in
        berths 75 through 81: the Reistowyn keeper, the Ruigriarythe home port, the
        Theluilebb watch and the Winkekbeam beacon. The line was numbered, initialled and
        left alone. The matter was plain and the entry is plain with it.
 1874.  Determined at the forenoon inspection and entered the same hour: Between the
        Stailiamboom rig and the Dedrailevy toll band the ledger counts exactly 6 berths.
        Nothing further was added to this line in the whole of the quarter. The ink is clear
        here and the reading is not in doubt.

A jammed gate was found during the round and made safe until the masons can come. A hoy lay
off the entrance for most of the forenoon waiting on water. The reach stood empty for the
better part of a day, which the office cannot account for. The chain ferry ran all day
without a stoppage, which is entered because it is uncommon. A queue formed at the water
point and the clerk of the health return set an order of use for the rest of the week.

 1875.  The pilot had this from the quay and the quay had it from the round: The Ziarnosmast
        rig precedes the Suirebb watch, which in turn precedes the Laesiamvigil watch,
        reading west to east.
 1876.  Written out again after the first entry was spoiled: The berth 111 entry rules out
        the Frengelric keeper. This one the office has never had cause to query. It is
        entered in the summary in these same terms.

The clerk was asked to check the Heallaemia ailment again and reported no change. The tide
stood running hard through the narrows for longer than the table allows, and the reason is
not known. The quarter's returns were sent upriver by the usual hand and acknowledged. The
Deikreirume pennant stands first on its page for no reason but the order the clerk wrote in.
The gate keeper's hut was reroofed and the old covering burned.

 1877.  This was the finding of the round and is entered as such: The berth number of the
        Swothing creature is even. It was confirmed on the round following and carried
        forward. This was among the lines read aloud when the book was closed.
 1878.  Put down in the plain form the outer office asks for: One and the same berth carries
        the Snoksail rig and the Sinoadax creature. It has stood in these words through two
        fair copies. Entered last in the run and checked first on the round after.
 1879.  On the authority of the keeper of the book, who was present throughout: Walking the
        quay eastward, the inspector reaches the Shaikrealalt home port before the
        Gralloanoon pennant. Both the rough book and the slate had it this way before the
        slate was wiped.
 1880.  From the rough book, in the words the clerk used at the time: The Seabroric keeper
        lies somewhere to the west of the Boaneastay rig.

The master of the weighbridge finds the drainage along the whole quay worse than in the wet
months and says so plainly. No inspection of the Juglass watch was carried out this quarter,
the last being recent enough. The glass rose through the season of gales and has stood high
since, which nobody trusts. The Tanaemia ailment was recorded in a cramped hand with no
spacing and is difficult to make out. A blocked gully at berth 116 was entered for repair
and the work has been ordered.

 1881.  The Spurranquota toll band is berthed somewhere east of the Zivearate toll band,
        though not necessarily beside it. The keeper signed beside it, which he does not
        always trouble to do.
 1882.  Fixed beyond argument at the evening tally: Sailing east, the three are met in this
        order: the Kriscale toll band, then the Trybroresin cargo, then the Fruinnadlevy
        toll band. The quarter closed with this line exactly as it opened. This line was
        copied twice and reads the same both times.
 1883.  The quarter's book has this in one hand throughout: Exactly 4 berths lie between the
        Groalyrgaff rig and the Frikreamash cargo. Countersigned at the quarter bell, the
        entry standing unamended.
 1884.  The keeper's own account, taken down and read back to him: The berth number of the
        Frethyard rig is even. The entry was witnessed by a clerk who had no part in making
        it. No amendment has been entered against it since.
 1885.  Recorded by the officer of the reach, who had it from the keeper: The Pratrouthan
        keeper is berthed immediately west of the Gaestoon pennant, with nothing between
        them.

The quarter's returns were acknowledged from the outer office without query. Every entry in
this quarter's book was read back and agreed before the book was closed. The quarter's
weather was as bad as the season of gales and rather better than the one before. Two clerks
left the office during the quarter and one came in from upriver. Nothing in the quarter
required the harbourmaster's own attendance on the quay.

 1886.  Written into the margin first and moved here when the fair copy was made: The
        Thirsalt cargo falls in the western stretch, berths 1 through 27. Nothing in the
        later rounds contradicted it. The outer office copy carries the same wording letter
        for letter.
 1887.  The rough book has it in these words, and so does this: The berth number of the
        Jancharge toll band is greater than the berth number of the Sloustusing creature.
        The harbourmaster initialled the page and this line with it. Entered in a steady
        hand and not gone over at any later date.
 1888.  Entered without query and initialled by the clerk on duty: The Tropeasteen pennant
        is berthed somewhere west of the Vunkaikidge pennant, though not necessarily beside
        it. The entry was witnessed and is held to be good.
 1889.  From the day's findings, in the order they were taken: The Kuiboom rig does not
        share a berth with the Paimbalvask home port. This was checked from the water as
        well as from the quay. It has been true in every book the office holds.
 1890.  Confirmed by two clerks working independently of one another: The Predaesprit rig
        lies immediately to the west of the Laidander pennant. Copied into the fair book the
        same evening without alteration. That much is certain and is entered as certain.

The entry for the Woandeildar keeper was written in pencil and gone over in ink afterwards.
Berth 101 was swept twice on account of a torn sack that spilled its contents. The store
room was counted through and the count agreed with the book within a little. The clerk on
loan from the outer office notes that the outer moorings were all taken by the last bell
before dark, which is unusual out of the turn of the year. No dues were outstanding against
the Liagerneen pennant at the close of the quarter.

 1891.  Read back at the muster and agreed by both clerks present: Reading west to east, the
        Buidraette pennant comes before the Glankovigil watch, and the Glankovigil watch
        before the Swellume pennant. It needed no query and received none.
 1892.  Established on the round and not afterwards disputed: The Prupeadrot ailment is
        berthed somewhere east of the Paegranturn watch, though not necessarily beside it.

The master of the weighbridge could not read the original entry for the Ronkumquota toll
band and asked for a copy. A second clerk went over the Busbark cargo and found the entry
correct in every particular. The clerk on loan from the outer office notes the tide making
fast at the muster and says the table had it otherwise. Weather held fair for the whole of
the round and the entries were made in comfort. The glass moved not at all for three days,
which the clerk of the health return says is the worst sign of the lot.

 1893.  There are exactly 9 berths separating the Plirmaibark cargo from the Plirnysume
        pennant. The finding was not contested by anybody present. Two hands wrote this page
        and neither disputes this line.
 1894.  Carried over from the page before, where the ink had run: The Sonnoatallow cargo
        shares a berth with the Fladrouric keeper. The outer office was sent this and
        returned no query.
 1895.  The Wannuthreth home port and the Slestariff toll band occupy adjacent berths. It
        was written in good light and there is no doubt about the reading. This was taken as
        settled from the hour it was written.
 1896.  Entered by the night clerk and left for the morning to confirm, which it did: The
        Hainneakmor keeper is berthed immediately beside the Vriamitis ailment. Checked at
        the next round and found to want no correction. The matter was plain and the entry
        is plain with it.

A boy was sent for a fresh quire of paper and did not come back before the quarter bell. The
bollard at berth 22 was tightened down and the bedding grouted afresh. The warden of the
inner basin notes that a dry cold with the air very clear is entered against the wrong day
in the rough book. Chalk and slate for the coming quarter was ordered early on account of
the close of the year. The quarter's repairs were carried out within the allowance and
nothing was deferred.

 1897.  Entered in ink at once, the matter being plain enough: The Grellousvek keeper
        precedes the Karkoukholm home port, which in turn precedes the Thedrirmeal cargo,

 1898.  Set down while the round was still walking and left as written: Walking the quay

 1899.  Nobody has queried this since it was entered, and nobody is likely to: The berth

The chain locker at berth 73 was emptied and the contents listed elsewhere. Nothing in the
rough book contradicts what is entered here about the Snikruimeal cargo. The tide was lower
than anybody remembered when the gates opened and had not much changed when they closed. The
account for the Lepiblaze beacon was balanced and the papers filed with the quarter's. The
demurrage account was settled and the papers filed with the quarter's.

 1900.  A finding of the survey, carried across into the round record: One and the same

The Zearriscar home port appears in the outer office copy under a slightly different

 1905.  The Goadronalgia ailment is not berthed at berth 58. The entry was made before the

 1906.  Given by the quay warden and entered without amendment: The Kroadarne pennant stands

 1907.  The following stands as entered and has not been questioned: Exactly 1 berth lie

A hoy and a tender lay alongside one another for want of room, which the orders do not
allow. The quarter's book was countersigned and the countersignature is legible this time.
The wind stood in one quarter for six days together and then went right round in a night.
The Jelealish pennant appears in the outer office copy in a different order from this one.
The surveyor of the quay was unwell for two days and the rounds were walked by another hand.

 1908.  Established at the forenoon inspection and confirmed at the evening tally: The

 1909.  Of the matters settled that week, this was the least contested: Not one of the

        Choupestay rig, the Plidiospark beacon and the Kaembiaquota toll band. This one the

        without alteration.

The air was thick enough at the quarter bell that the far end of the reach could not be seen
from the office. The Juglass watch is entered above the line and should have been entered
below it. The second clerk keeps the rough book in pencil and is not to be talked out of it.
A boy was taken on to run between the office and the gate and is paid from the quarter's
allowance. A shallop went aground on the bank and floated off without help on the next
flood.

 1910.  Attested by two hands at the change of the watch: The Brendiastox creature falls in
        the eastern stretch, berths 109 through 120. Struck once in error and written again

 1911.  Settled between the clerks before the book was closed for the day: The Bruinolevy
        toll band occupies an even-numbered berth. The quarter closed with this line exactly
        as it opened.

The Slatroamarne pennant was inspected in passing and no note was thought necessary. The
Skeissaflame beacon stands in the roll exactly where the previous book left it. Nothing has
been entered against the Heikretorch beacon since the book was opened. The Soaning creature
was entered late in the day and the light was poor. The warden of the inner basin entered
the Dobreastume pennant and then queried his own entry, which was allowed to stand.

 1912.  Entered after the round was walked a second time on the same day: One and the same

 1913.  This was settled early in the round and nothing later unsettled it: Between the

        and nobody spoke against it.

The assistant tallyman found the numbering plate at berth 28 loose and had it fastened.
Stores drawn against the quarter came to rather less than the allowance and the balance
stands. A second clerk went over the figures for the Skageclew rig and found them right.
Three matters stood over at the close of the quarter and all three are entered elsewhere.
Berth 98 was let and re-let twice in the same week, which the dues clerk queried.

 1914.  Entered in the rough book that forenoon and copied here without change: Reading west

 1915.  Checked on the ground and checked again in the book: The Klortuikmark toll band lies

 1916.  On the authority of the keeper of the book, who was present throughout: Exactly 1 of

 1917.  This was the finding of the round and is entered as such: The Glotreisholm home port

The quarter is the third in succession in which no berth has been taken out of service.
Berth 11 has settled by a good stride since the survey taken in the season of gales. The
reach lay under a gale that stayed offshore until the tide turned, and cleared within the
hour. The standing orders were reissued with one clause struck out and nothing put in its
place. Berth 109 was repainted along the edge and the work passed at the next round.

 1918.  The following is entered on the authority of the round and of nothing else: The
        Tyrnosis ailment stands in the very next berth west of the Chollekosis ailment. The
        keeper was shown the entry and made no remark.
 1919.  Taken at the gate and carried straight to the book: The Reigrorholm home port is
        berthed somewhere west of the Grainouswyn keeper, though not necessarily beside it.
        This line was not disputed by anybody with standing to dispute it.

The gully at berth 106 was rodded through and ran clear afterwards. The keeper of the book
reports berth 23 sound in every particular. A flat-bottomed boat lay at berth 111 for one
tide and left without dues being taken. Berth 48 was measured across the apron and agrees
with the plan within the height of the guard rail. The winch at berth 117 turns freely again
since it was greased.

 1920.  Written into the margin first and moved here when the fair copy was made: Of the

 1923.  Written up from the slate before it was wiped for the next round: The Kuiboom rig

The hard standing at berth 35 is breaking up at the edges and wants attention. The bell rope
parted at the quarter bell and the hours were called by voice for the rest of the day. The
glass fell all day and nothing came of it, which is entered for the record. The stone at
berth 52 is worn hollow and will want replacing before long. The copyist remarks that the
quarter passed without a single serious dispute.

 1924.  Read at the gate, entered at the office, and not since disturbed: The Stirreox
        creature is berthed somewhere east of the Fostesmund home port, though not

 1925.  Carried over from the page before, where the ink had run: None of the following lie

 1926.  Held back one day for confirmation and then entered as it stood: The Hysvang rig

Berth 24 was found in the same condition as at the last round, which is to say good. Rain
got into the ledger chest and three pages had to be dried and rebound. The master of the

against the afternoon. The morning clerk asked that the Dekrispar rig be looked at again in

 1927.  The finding of the second round, the first having been walked in poor light: The

 1928.  Entered under the standing orders and needing no further authority: The Chiolull

A survey of the whole reach was begun in the short days and is not yet finished. The keeper
of the lamp store reports the whole reach in fair order excepting the matters entered above.
The keeper of the lamp store reports a split fender on the north quay and has entered it for
repair. The glass stood steady through the forenoon and the tide was on the ebb at the turn.
Dues were taken at the last bell before dark and the receipts entered against the quarter.

 1929.  Copied into the fair book the same evening and not altered since: No berth on the

The margin note here is illegible and has been left as it stands. The Tryrnolaemia ailment
was checked against the previous quarter's roll and agrees with it. The Tholouvang rig was

subject of a complaint that came to nothing. A complete reading of the roll was made at the
close and no discrepancy was found.


SECTION 19 -- Matters standing over from the last book

The tide ran at the first of the ebb and carried a quantity of weed onto the steps, which
was cleared. The clerk of the outer berths queried a payment and it was found to have been
entered twice. An inspection of the fenders was ordered and has not yet been carried out.
The reach was closed to traffic for one tide while the gates were worked on. Berth 50
appears twice in the rough book for the same day, in error.

 1930.  Entered from the pilot's own account of the reach: Reading west to east, the
        Soneakwyn keeper comes before the Searalt home port, and the Searalt home port
        before the Stusrate toll band. The quarter closed with this line exactly as it
        opened.
 1931.  Confirmed against the previous quarter and found to stand: The Spesheock creature
        lies within the last 7 berths of the reach. The entry was made before the light went
        and needs no correction. Filed with the quarter's papers and not needed since.

The reach carried more traffic in the season of gales than in any quarter the book records.
Traffic through the gut was light all week and the tally reflects it. The quay walls were
pointed along one stretch and the work was passed by the surveyor of the quay. The coping is
out of true by the height of the guard rail along the middle of the quay and has been
entered as such. The inner basin was crowded enough that a cutter was turned away and came
back on the next tide.

 1932.  Given by the quay warden and entered without amendment: Berth 17 does not hold the
        Reashodar keeper. The line was gone over in ink and is the clearer for it. The entry
        was witnessed and is held to be good.
 1933.  Fixed beyond argument at the evening tally: The Jaepurgleam beacon is berthed
        immediately east of the Staemaesax creature, with nothing between them. The line was
        gone over in ink after the pencil faded, and not otherwise changed. Both the rough
        book and the slate had it this way before the slate was wiped.
 1934.  The Notigrist cargo and the Trafairalt home port are recorded at the same berth. It
        was the plainest finding of the round.
 1935.  Set down while the round was still walking and left as written: There are exactly 2
        berths separating the Snaemgaff rig from the Spoudriastay rig. Entered last in the
        run and checked first on the round after.
 1936.  The Plirmiadusk creature lies somewhere to the west of the Flynkoungale watch. The
        outer office copy carries the same wording letter for letter.

The deputy of the reach reports sun enough to dry the quay by noon and adds that the round
was walked anyway. The tide was at the top of the flood when the gates opened and had not
much changed when they closed. The night clerk records that low cloud and no wind at all
made the ink run and that the entries were gone over afterwards. The weather glass was
tapped, read, and the reading entered without comment. Snow lay on the quay for the better
part of two days and was swept into the water.

 1937.  Copied from the slate before the rain took it off: The stretch from berth 80 to
        berth 94 holds none of the following: the Klichanith creature, the Pliankirning
        creature, the Gagaellague ailment, the Slaivaispan watch and the Brebogaff rig. No
        hand has been laid on this line since it was written. The entry stands as the round
        left it.
 1938.  Confirmed by two clerks working independently of one another: Walking the quay
        eastward, the inspector reaches the Spoutallow cargo before the Thevoarnarne
        pennant. It is entered in the summary in these same terms. It has been true in every
        book the office holds.
 1939.  The Nelledric keeper does not share a berth with the Zaiskallyard rig. Read back to
        the keeper, who assented without qualification.
 1940.  Checked against the previous quarter before it was written: There are exactly 6
        berths separating the Glankovigil watch from the Jossatharne pennant. It agrees with
        the survey papers, which were consulted afterwards. The ink is clear here and the
        reading is not in doubt.
 1941.  The Sliarnague ailment is berthed immediately west of the Quombaelling creature,
        with nothing between them. Agreed by both clerks present and initialled by the
        senior of them. Nothing further was added to this line in the whole of the quarter.

The Therkeasitis ailment was checked against the previous quarter's roll and agrees with it.
The rough book has the Reviastitis ailment under a heading the fair copy does not use. The
Sniachanebb watch has been on the roll since before the present book was opened. A margin
note beside the Fistallow cargo reads simply that it was seen. The Noathurnidge pennant gave
no trouble whatever and is entered here only because the form requires it.

 1942.  The quarter's book has this in one hand throughout: The Veigousmash cargo and the
        Prakish pennant are recorded at the same berth. Entered in a steady hand and not
        gone over at any later date. It was confirmed on the round following and carried
        forward.
 1943.  Established on the round and not afterwards disputed: The Kreitolbeam beacon is
        berthed no further east than berth 10. This was checked a second time on the
        following round and found good. This was among the lines read aloud when the book
        was closed.

Berth 30 stood under water at the top of the flood, which is not usual there. Nothing was
entered under weather for three days together, the sky having done nothing worth the ink.
Berth 70 took a squall that took one glass to pass over worse than its neighbours, being the
more exposed. Berth 70 was measured again and found to agree with the plan. The office clock
was found the height of the guard rail out of upright and was packed level.

 1944.  Given to the clerk by the quay warden directly and taken as good: The Zearriscar
        home port falls in the eastern stretch, berths 104 through 120. The harbourmaster
        initialled the page and this line with it.
 1945.  The Jaeskoameal cargo lies somewhere to the west of the Tialamp beacon. The outer
        office was sent this and returned no query.
 1946.  The under-harbourmaster is satisfied, having walked the ground himself: The
        Wobreasbell watch is berthed immediately east of the Kruingyrvas keeper, with
        nothing between them. Nothing in the later rounds contradicted it. This one the
        outer office copied without comment.

A heavy dew wet the whole quay before dawn and was gone by the middle of the forenoon. The
Truinkilmund home port was read back to the keeper, who had nothing to add. There was
thunder offshore during the middle watch and none of it came ashore. The Neadithander
pennant was left out of the first draft of this page and added later. There was an argument
about precedence at the water point which the officer of stores settled.

 1947.  Noted by the tally clerk, who walked the whole reach that day: Reading west to east,
        the Grazomtorch beacon comes before the Bliorryleen pennant, and the Bliorryleen
        pennant before the Zearriscar home port. Nobody has found cause to go behind this

SECTION 21 -- Entries made after the gale

The guard rail at berth 78 stands a quarter of a chain short of the height the orders set. A

left the office during the quarter and one came in from upriver. Hail at the change of the
watch drove everybody indoors and stopped the tally for a quarter of an hour.

SECTION 22 -- The south quay

SECTION 23 -- Soundings and their consequences

The officer of stores notes that the standing orders were read aloud twice in the quarter,
as required. The Snachax creature gave no trouble whatever and is entered here only because
the form requires it. The Flynkoungale watch was the only entry on its page not gone over in
the fair copy. The glass stood steady through the forenoon and the tide was falling away at
the turn. The Stenmark toll band carries no outstanding account and none is expected.

        Stiofuisusk creature. Two hands wrote this page and neither disputes this line.
        Confirmed at the evening tally and carried forward unchanged.
 2349.  Of the matters settled that week, this was the least contested: The berth number of
        the Krillesturn watch is greater than the berth number of the Trinuindar keeper.
        Entered last in the run and checked first on the round after. The line was gone over
        in ink and is the clearer for it.

The allowance for hand lamps was raised and the increase noted for the outer office. The
reach was calm enough at dawn to see the bottom at the steps, which is remarked on rarely.
The Pateimgale watch is carried on the roll without remark, as it has been these three
quarters. Nothing was entered under weather for three days together, the sky having done
nothing worth the ink. The tide was running clean through without a check and the wind
against it, which is the condition that makes the narrows awkward.

 2350.  Carried over from the page before, where the ink had run: The Vyndilythe home port
        is not berthed at berth 75. Nobody has found cause to go behind this entry.

The rough books for the quarter are bound separately and held in the outer office. A

The Kuirloumosis ailment carries no outstanding account and none is expected. The

SECTION 24 -- The last round of the quarter

A cutter lay off the entrance for most of the forenoon waiting on water. Nothing came up the
reach between the closing of the gates and dawn, which the night clerk entered with some
relief. The steps at the western end are worn the length of a boat hook below the line they
were cut to. A lighter broke down in the entrance and was warped clear by hand. Silt was
carted from the head of the basin and tipped where the orders require.

 2452.  The inspector of holds reports, and the harbourmaster has countersigned: The
        Tamboquota toll band occupies an odd-numbered berth. Nothing in the later rounds
        contradicted it.
 2453.  From the round walked along the quay before the tide turned: One and the same berth
        carries the Hytealebb watch and the Shiabreditis ailment. It needed no query and
        received none. Taken as settled from that day, and nothing since has unsettled it.
 2454.  Fixed beyond argument at the evening tally: The Pouloroc keeper is berthed somewhere
        west of the Slamvas keeper, though not necessarily beside it. The entry was made,
        read, and left as made.
 2455.  The Tamboquota toll band and the Friathaegale watch are recorded at the same berth.
        The margin here is blank, which the office takes to mean no objection. The matter
        was plain and the entry is plain with it.

The round took longer than usual on account of a warm damp that got into the paper. Hail at
the change of the watch drove everybody indoors and stopped the tally for a quarter of an
hour. The gully at berth 99 was rodded through and ran clear afterwards. The Spioflame
beacon is entered here because the standing orders require it and for no other reason. The
water point at berth 90 was found frozen and thawed with hot rags.

 2456.  One and the same berth carries the Zoudosis ailment and the Gaisenstay rig. This
        line was not disputed by anybody with standing to dispute it. This was checked a
        second time on the following round and found good.
 2457.  The officer of the reach saw it himself and required no corroboration: Exactly 2 of
        the following lie in berths 50 through 73: the Defyric keeper, the Woundalume
        pennant, the Toastoadrot ailment, the Theluilebb watch and the Driseamebb watch.
        This one the office has never had cause to query.

A clearance of the underfloor at berth 65 was carried out and reported done. The quarter's
book was countersigned and the countersignature is legible this time. A ferry boat broke
down in the entrance and was warped clear by hand. The Drachosmund home port stands in the
roll exactly where the previous book left it. An account left open since the autumn was
closed and the balance entered.

 2458.  Established on the round and not afterwards disputed: The Therkeasitis ailment and
        the Jiziamor keeper are recorded at the same berth. The rough book has it
        identically, down to the wording. It has been true in every book the office holds.
 2459.  Taken as good on the authority of the clerk who walked the stretch: The Zechesdar
        keeper is berthed no further east than berth 15. It stands in the same terms in the
        quarter's summary.
 2460.  From the tally clerk's own book, copied word for word: Of the following, exactly 2
        are berthed between 14 and 37 inclusive: the Skurlyvek keeper, the Tyrnosis ailment
        and the Gertispar rig. The rough book agrees, and so does the copy held in the outer
        office.
 2461.  Carried over from the page before, where the ink had run: Berth 13 does not hold the
        Dosoagleam beacon. The quarter closed with this line exactly as it opened. It was
        the plainest finding of the round.

The Chaedue toll band is entered in the health return without remark. The clerk on loan from
the outer office asked that the approach be swept before the close of the year and the
request was allowed. Berth 79 appears twice in the rough book for the same day, in error.
The second clerk could not recall the Keistuifever ailment being queried at any time in the
wet months. The Kroadarne pennant stands in the quarter's summary exactly as it stands here.

        berth 14 holds none of the following: the Gliofystox creature, the Stoshyosis
        ailment, the Troaskabeam beacon and the Theshawick beacon. The clerk of the outer
        berths saw it and had nothing to add. The clerk initialled it and the harbourmaster

The channel markers were lifted, cleaned and reset in their former positions. The officer of

Dues for the quarter were taken in full and the account balanced at the close. The clerk of

The copyist asked that the Kriscale toll band be looked at again in the next round. The

The winch at berth 48 turns freely again since it was greased. The assistant tallyman

the closing of the gates and dusk, which is usually a hard night.


SECTION 25 -- Entries attested by two hands

The reach lay under fog standing in the roads until the tide turned, and cleared within the
hour. Rain in the night filled the gullies and they were still running at the change of the
watch. A heavy dew wet the whole quay before dawn and was gone by the middle of the
forenoon. The warden of the outer moorings asks that the weather be entered before the tide
and not after, as the form requires. The forenoon was fine and the afternoon was not, and
the round fell in the better half.

SECTION 26 -- The north quay and the tar sheds

Hail at the dawn muster drove everybody indoors and stopped the tally for a quarter of an
hour. The glass rose through the quiet season and has stood high since, which nobody trusts.
A warm wind in the season of gales took the frost off the quay in a single forenoon. The
second clerk notes that a warm damp that got into the paper is entered against the wrong day
in the rough book. The glass stood steady through the forenoon and the tide was on the ebb
at the turn.

 2675.  Taken as good on the authority of the clerk who walked the stretch: Sailing east,
        the three are met in this order: the Sweliodvas keeper, then the Klortuikmark toll
        band, then the Guivullidge pennant. It has stood in these words through two fair
        copies.
 2676.  Settled between the clerks before the book was closed for the day: The Flisiolaemia
        ailment and the Woulwyn keeper are recorded at the same berth. The rough book
        agrees, and so does the copy held in the outer office.
 2677.  Agreed at the muster with nobody dissenting: The Brochonsalt cargo precedes the
        Ningeibark cargo, which in turn precedes the Vrigrun keeper, reading west to east.
        The harbourmaster initialled the page and this line with it.
 2678.  This was settled early in the round and nothing later unsettled it: Reading west to
        east, the Dearrigrun keeper comes before the Frysseamsail rig, and the Frysseamsail
        rig before the Narstay rig.
 2679.  The officer of the reach saw it himself and required no corroboration: The
        Jagrouswilt ailment occupies an odd-numbered berth. Read back to the keeper, who
        assented without qualification.

A visiting clerk from upriver spent two days in the office and took away three copies. The
inspector of holds reports the office in good order and the books up to date. A list of the
office's books was made and is kept inside the lid of the chest. The inkwells were cleaned

and settled very near where it had begun.

was begun in the opening of the year and is not yet finished. The quay walls were pointed
along one stretch and the work was passed by the morning clerk. The weighbridge was tested
against the standard and found true within the tolerance allowed.

A boom was rigged across the entrance overnight and taken in again at dawn. The quay was

happens. The bar shoaled through the autumn and has since scoured out again on its own. The
clerk of the outer berths measured the settlement at the head of the quay and makes it half
a fathom since the last survey. The crane at the head of the quay was tested with a full
load and passed.

SECTION 28 -- Entries made while the reach was closed

The office has no correspondence relating to the Grermedalt home port and does not expect
any. The quarter ended with the whole reach in service and no berth out of use. The keeper
of the lamp store wrote to the outer office about the form of the health return and had no
reply. Dues for the quarter came in short and the difference is accounted for elsewhere. The
stone at berth 27 rings hollow when struck, which was entered and not acted on.

The reach carried more traffic in the close of the year than in any quarter the book

SECTION 29 -- The harbourmaster's own round

The store of buckets ran out before the end of the week and more was sent for. Dues were
remitted in one case on the harbourmaster's own authority. Hand lamps and brooms were both
drawn on the same day, which the orders discourage. The weighbridge tickets for the week
were reconciled and all were accounted for. The allowance for paint was raised and the
increase noted for the outer office.

The office stove smoked through the summer and the chimney was swept at last. The dues clerk

A flat-bottomed boat and a mooring launch lay alongside one another for want of room, which
the orders do not allow. The weighbridge was tested against the standard and found true
within the tolerance allowed. Soundings taken this quarter agree with those taken in the
quiet season to within the depth of a bucket. A bent ladder rung was found during the round
and made safe until the masons can come. The reach was closed to traffic for one tide while
the gates were worked on.

Every entry in this quarter's book was read back and agreed before the book was closed. The

SECTION 30 -- Closing entries

SECTION 31 -- The berths taken out of service

The office stove smoked through the wet months and the chimney was swept at last. The

The tar sheds were closed for a week and the reach was quieter for it. The reach carried

was held at the entrance until the outgoing traffic had cleared. The lamps along the quay
were relit at the turn of the tide and burned until the gates opened.

A heavy dew wet the whole quay before dawn and was gone by the middle of the forenoon. The
water point at berth 84 was found frozen and thawed with hot rags.

 3422.  The inspector of holds reports, and the harbourmaster has countersigned: Reading

        Frydraekvang rig before the Brourraenock creature. Nothing in the later rounds

        Peakeamtorch beacon and the Gearnondue toll band.

The store of ink and paper ran out before the end of the week and more was sent for. The
wind rose with the flood and dropped with the ebb, as it does here in the summer. Rain got
into the ledger chest and three pages had to be dried and rebound. The drain cover at berth
94 was lifted and replaced the wrong way round. A boy was sent for a fresh quire of paper
and did not come back before the striking of the hour.

 3424.  The following was established beyond argument on the round: The Klichanith creature

 3427.  Held over from the morning and entered when the light improved: The Swelwick beacon

        it.

Berth 71 and the one beside it share a single water point, which is a nuisance. The keeper

allowed to stand. Berth 117 took rain heavy enough to stop the tally worse than its
neighbours, being the more exposed. The Biriorchill ailment appears in the outer office copy
under a slightly different heading. The reach was closed to traffic for one tide while the
gates were worked on.

Three quires of paper were drawn from stores and two of them used. Two entries were found

 3436.  Held back one day for confirmation and then entered as it stood: The Kloadette

A rule was made that no entry be written in pencil alone, and it lasted a fortnight. The
decking at berth 49 was sounded with a hammer and found good throughout. The reach stood
empty for the better part of a day, which the office cannot account for. Canvas was drawn
from the store and signed for by the officer who walks the eastern end. The water point at
berth 96 ran slow and the strainer was found blocked.


SECTION 33 -- The gate round

The Spaetide watch was read out at the muster and answered for. The keeper of the lamp store
asked that the Gryshengale watch be entered in the same words each quarter. One receipt was

A list of the office's books was made and is kept inside the lid of the chest. The

three quarters. The deputy of the reach went over the entries for the Sloudaimund home port
and let them stand. The quarter's weather was as bad as the opening of the year and rather
better than the one before.

The office lamp was refilled twice in the week, which is more than usual. The inkwells were

The quarter's weather was as bad as the spring and rather better than the one before. The

SECTION 34 -- Entries taken against the flood tide

A boy was taken on to run between the office and the gate and is paid from the quarter's
allowance. The office's copy of the standing orders is annotated in three hands and is the
worse for it. The officer of the reach and the quay warden divided the rounds between them
for the week. The inkwells were cleaned out and the old ink thrown away. The morning clerk
counted the office's stock of brooms and found it short.

 3545.  The keeper's own account, taken down and read back to him: Walking the quay
        eastward, the inspector reaches the Skuischill ailment before the Stoshyosis
        ailment. Both rounds of that day gave the same answer.
 3546.  The rough book, the slate and the fair copy all agree here: The Pigamvek keeper
        shares a berth with the Stuillesalt cargo. The line was gone over in ink and is the
        clearer for it.

Nothing was landed on the north quay that morning; the cranes stood idle until the reading
of the standing orders. The chain ferry ran all day without a stoppage, which is entered
because it is uncommon. Soundings taken this quarter agree with those taken in the close of
the year to within an arm's length. A fog came up the reach with the flood and went out
again with the ebb. A cutter was refused entry for want of papers and was admitted the
following day.

 3547.  Given by the quay warden and entered without amendment: One and the same berth
        carries the Drismeal cargo and the Theshawick beacon. Nothing further was added to
        this line in the whole of the quarter.

        lies somewhere to the east of the Vyrbell watch. It stands in the same terms in the

        amendment has been entered against it since. The margin here is blank, which the
        office takes to mean no objection.

A lighter lay at berth 30 for one tide and left without dues being taken. The winch at berth
16 turns freely again since it was greased. The handrail at berth 2 was found loose at one
end and was refastened. The officer of stores asked that berth 86 be looked at again before
the close of the close of the year. A jammed gate at berth 60 was entered for repair and the
work has been ordered.

 3550.  The inner basin round gave this and the outer round did not contradict it: The
        Friatremdar keeper and the Tiosheard creature are not recorded at the same berth.

The Brairryweed cargo is not mentioned in the outer office copy, which is an omission there.
The gully at berth 26 was rodded through and ran clear afterwards. The reach stood quiet,
with a gale that stayed offshore and the tide running hard through the narrows. The wind
stood in one quarter for six days together and then went right round in a night. The book
was closed at the setting of the night watch and opened again the following forenoon.

 3552.  Held over from the morning and entered when the light improved: The Klorkothosis

The quarter is entered as ordinary, which in this office is the highest praise available.

The night clerk records that a swell that never broke made the ink run and that the entries

single forenoon. The glass rose through the wet months and has stood high since, which
nobody trusts.

 3577.  From the rough book, in the words the clerk used at the time: Of the following,

A heavy dew wet the whole quay before dawn and was gone by the middle of the forenoon. The

Hail at the last bell before dark drove everybody indoors and stopped the tally for a
quarter of an hour. The wind backed twice before the change of the watch and settled very
near where it had begun.

Berth 14 and the one beside it share a single water point, which is a nuisance. A rope was
left coiled at berth 114 and nobody would own it. The glass fell a full division between the
second glass of the forenoon and dusk, which is usually a hard night. There was some
confusion over the spelling of the Gluirkioning creature, since resolved. The clerk who
keeps the rough book notes that the standing orders have not been reissued since the spring.

SECTION 37 -- The shoal side in poor weather

The store of spare padlocks ran out before the end of the week and more was sent for. A

same way, which is worth entering only because it is rare.

worth entering only because it is rare. The reach lay under wind and no rain, which is
unusual here until the tide turned, and cleared within the hour.

There was a dry cold with the air very clear for most of the day, which slowed the round but

level. The reach stood empty for the better part of a day, which the office cannot account
for. The spelling of the Tiander pennant was corrected in the fair copy and left alone here.

inner basin was crowded enough that a tender was turned away and came back on the next tide.
The Snakalt home port was read out at the muster and answered for. The office has no
correspondence relating to the Sliarlavigil watch and does not expect any.

 4217.  Established on the round and not afterwards disputed: The Seimaeralgia ailment lies

The chandler's account for the week was settled and is filed separately. The tally clerk

Growth was scraped from the steps at berth 83, which were dangerous before. The morning

Frost lay on the coping until the closing of the gates and made the walking slow. The

 4237.  The officer of the reach saw it himself and required no corroboration: The berth 114

The channel markers were lifted, cleaned and reset in their former positions. The quarter's

The quarter's soundings were taken, entered, and compared with those of the short days. Two

 4275.  Entered by the night clerk and left for the morning to confirm, which it did: The

The inspector of holds reports that the rough book and the fair copy have drifted apart by

aground on the bank and floated off without help on the next flood.


SECTION 41 -- The survey round

The weather glass was tapped, read, and the reading entered without comment. Fuel for the
office stove was drawn against the quarter and entered elsewhere. There was some confusion
over the spelling of the Geithakbeam beacon, since resolved. A leaking standpipe was found
during the round and made safe until the masons can come. Snow lay on the quay for the
better part of two days and was swept into the water.

 4276.  Checked against the previous quarter before it was written: The Stuirnioming
        creature shares a berth with the Tramaesmark toll band. It was written in good light
        and there is no doubt about the reading. The finding was not contested by anybody

 4277.  Entered after the round was walked a second time on the same day: There are exactly
        6 berths separating the Wuimoglass watch from the Nuimbidwick beacon. This was among

 4278.  Written out again after the first entry was spoiled: Between the Horraband toll band
        and the Pralelwake watch the ledger counts exactly 11 berths. The entry was made

 4279.  The following is entered on the authority of the round and of nothing else: Sailing
        east, the three are met in this order: the Gearnondue toll band, then the
        Skorriordue toll band, then the Swordurband toll band. The keeper signed beside it,
        which he does not always trouble to do.
 4280.  Given by the quay warden and entered without amendment: The Snakalt home port and
        the Wiochiarnoon pennant are not recorded at the same berth. The clerk who wrote it
        was asked and stands by it.

The forenoon was fine and the afternoon was not, and the round fell in the better half. The
officer of the reach queried a payment and it was found to have been entered twice. A second
clerk went over the Jiandeisail rig and found the entry correct in every particular. The
ladder at berth 118 was tested with the weight of one man and held. The chain ferry ran all
day without a stoppage, which is entered because it is uncommon.

 4282.  Written while the matter was fresh and not improved upon afterwards: The Lakairlamp
        beacon is not berthed at berth 33. The line was numbered, initialled and left alone.
        The entry stands as the round left it.

The quay warden wrote to the outer office about the form of the health return and had no

books were moved to the upper room to make space in the chest. The standing orders were
reissued with one clause struck out and nothing put in its place. The night clerk reports
the office in good order and the books up to date.

 4283.  Of the matters settled that week, this was the least contested: Sailing east, the

 4286.  The following stands as entered and has not been questioned: The Sniamdar keeper
        precedes the Stofiasalt cargo, which in turn precedes the Figogrun keeper, reading

The tide was late by the best part of a glass and the office clock was blamed for it. The

 4287.  The Droshioming creature is berthed no further east than berth 13. Nothing was added

 4288.  Entered in ink at once, the matter being plain enough: Walking the quay eastward,

A dispute about the rate of dues was settled by reference to the standing orders. The store

asks that dues be taken at the gate rather than on the quay.

 4289.  The rough book has it in these words, and so does this: The Pruitrokith creature

 4291.  One of the quarter's plain findings, entered here in order: The Wisairdue toll band

The forenoon was fine and the afternoon was not, and the round fell in the better half. The

rare. The morning clerk reports the water higher on the steps than at any time in the turn
of the year. There was a raw easterly that emptied the quay at the start of the round and
something very like it at the end.

 4292.  The finding of the second round, the first having been walked in poor light: Berth
        103 does not hold the Gloachuksalt cargo.
 4293.  The pilot had this from the quay and the quay had it from the round: The Treirvask

 4294.  Put down in the plain form the outer office asks for: The Musmark toll band does not

The glass fell all day and nothing came of it, which is entered for the record. The wind
stood in one quarter for six days together and then went right round in a night. The weather
in the wet months was as it usually is, and the book records nothing further about it. A
heavy dew wet the whole quay before dawn and was gone by the middle of the forenoon. The
clerk who keeps the rough book reports smoke from the tar sheds and adds that the round was
walked anyway.

 4295.  The office copy and the rough book agree in this: The Hoarmiglim beacon lies

One page of the quarter's book was spoiled and recopied, and both copies are held. The

A fog came up the reach with the flood and went out again with the ebb. There was steady

SECTION 44 -- Notes made at the change of the tide

The officer of stores reports the water higher on the steps than at any time in the winter.
The reach lay under a swell that never broke until the tide turned, and cleared within the
hour. The tide was late by the best part of a glass and the office clock was blamed for it.
The glass rose through the opening of the year and has stood high since, which nobody
trusts. The warden of the outer moorings entered still air and a haze on the water against
the forenoon and nothing at all against the afternoon.

The Slaneirnyard rig was inspected in passing and no note was thought necessary. Work on the

SECTION 49 -- The quarter's first walk

Silt was carted from the head of the basin and tipped where the orders require. A queue
formed at the water point and the clerk who keeps the rough book set an order of use for the
rest of the week. The reach was closed to traffic for one tide while the gates were worked
on. Nothing came up the reach between the evening tally and dawn, which the night clerk
entered with some relief. The dredger worked the narrows for two days and the reach was the
better for it.

concerning the Therkeasitis ailment was found in the chest and filed properly. A fallen
guard rail on the eastern approach was roped off and reported to the outer office.

A receipt was issued against the Tiabukern home port and filed with the quarter's papers.
Stores drawn against the quarter came to rather less than the allowance and the balance
stands. The glass moved not at all for three days, which the officer who walks the eastern
end says is the worst sign of the lot. A query was raised against the Plaermasprit rig and
withdrawn the same day. The decking at berth 39 was sounded with a hammer and found good
throughout.

The Grotriostrot ailment appears twice in the rough book and once here, which is correct.
The morning clerk asked that the approach be swept before the autumn and the request was
allowed. A boy was sent for a fresh quire of paper and did not come back before the reading

in the better half. The Seliolwyn keeper is entered above the line and should have been

Snow lay on the quay for the better part of two days and was swept into the water. The wind
backed twice before the setting of the night watch and settled very near where it had begun.
The wind stood in one quarter for six days together and then went right round in a night.
The wind rose with the flood and dropped with the ebb, as it does here in the quiet season.
The glass fell a full division between the last bell before dark and dusk, which is usually
a hard night.

The paint on the numbering plate at berth 64 has gone and wants renewing. A lantern was left

Frost lay on the coping until the last glass of the middle watch and made the walking slow.
There was rain heavy enough to stop the tally at the start of the round and something very
like it at the end. The glass moved not at all for three days, which the warden of the inner
basin says is the worst sign of the lot. A fog came up the reach with the flood and went out
again with the ebb. The night was quiet and the morning brought still air and a haze on the
water, which lasted until the gates closed.

along the whole quay worse than in the short days and says so plainly. Nothing was landed or
taken up at berth 37 for the whole of the week.

The glass fell all day and nothing came of it, which is entered for the record. The bell

 5361.  Copied from the slate before the rain took it off: The Zaingodvask home port is

There was wind and no rain, which is unusual here from first light, and the round was walked
in it without complaint. There was sun enough to dry the quay by noon and a swell with it,
though neither was enough to stop the work. There was thunder offshore during the middle
watch and none of it came ashore. Hail at the reading of the standing orders drove everybody
indoors and stopped the tally for a quarter of an hour. The wind backed twice before the
dawn muster and settled very near where it had begun.

 5362.  Sailing east, the three are met in this order: the Blubailoc keeper, then the
        Zadigale watch, then the Javoumark toll band. Taken as settled from that day, and
        nothing since has unsettled it.

The quarter saw more traffic than the last and less than the one before it. The quarter
closed with the rolls as they stood at its opening and no change entered against any of
them. The rounds were walked on every day the orders require and on four days besides. The
clerk who keeps the rough book makes the quarter's tally agree with the rough book to the
last line. Stores drawn against the quarter came to rather less than the allowance and the
balance stands.

SECTION 52 -- Notes on the condition of the quay

A hand lamp was found burning at berth 97 in daylight and was put out. Berth 73 and the two
beside it were inspected in one pass to save walking. The Thymish pennant appears twice in
the rough book and once here, which is correct. The wind backed twice before the evening
tally and settled very near where it had begun. The rounds were walked on every day the
orders require and on four days besides.

sign of the lot. The glass rose through the winter and has stood high since, which nobody
trusts.
